verdict.rationale: Requesty offers an MCP Gateway that lets coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Roo Code, etc.) connect to MCP servers, with server registration, per-user keys, and analytics — this is a gateway/hub role rather than Requesty itself being an agent, so the axis applies and is documented. However, this is Requesty acting as an MCP aggregator/gateway for other agents to consume external tools, not clear evidence of a first-party 'official MCP server' endpoint that any external agent can connect to directly with a documented spec/URL, and there's no independent/hands-on corroboration. missing for 10: a concrete official MCP server endpoint/spec independent of the gateway product, and third-party or hands-on verification of the connection working.
